races.name: Watch Unibet Racing Postcast Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Le Beau Madrik
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with strong RPR credentials but carries concerns after a flat effort at 7-2 last time out 46 days ago.
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over hurdles until flat performance at Kelso; back from a break with yard riding high
runners_data.spotlight: Posted a very eyecatching RPR when making it 2-2 over hurdles at Newcastle in January (2m4f, soft; fine on good) and reportedly ran flat when only 7-2 for a Grade 2 at Kelso the following month; granted a break since then and he returns with his yard firing in winners left, right and centre.

runners_data.name: Matty's Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing first-time tongue-tie who has been keeping excellent company and showed smart form when beating a subsequent Grade 2 winner.
runners_data.comment: Took a notable scalp in November; major player provided the absence doesn't hold him back
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner who has been keeping good company over hurdles and, in a first-time tongue-tie, he comfortably accounted for subsequent Grade 2 winner Dalston Lad in a Doncaster maiden in late November (2m5f, good to soft); has since undergone a wind operation; major player provided the absence doesn't hold him back.

runners_data.name: Legendary Luke
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader whose stamina will be tested dropping back from 3m but has strong course knowledge from his Grade 2 effort here in February.
runners_data.comment: Relinquished his unbeaten record over hurdles in a 3m Grade 2 here in February
runners_data.spotlight: 3m point winner; relinquished his unbeaten record over hurdles in a 3m Grade 2 here in February but that was no backward step and he'd have finished closer than 12l to the winner Dalston Lad but for hitting two out; heading in the right direction and respected.

runners_data.name: Padre Arthur
runners_data.note: Henderson representative who improved significantly last time and should benefit from prominent tactics rather than being held up.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 15l into second at Kempton but the winner is useful and that was better
runners_data.spotlight: Only sixth in his first two races (debut was a bumper) but raised his profile when chasing home a talented and shorter-priced stablemate at Kempton in early February (2m5f, good to soft); he was 15l adrift but this 5yo no doubt has plenty more to offer.

runners_data.name: Intosomethinggood
runners_data.comment: 4-11 over hurdles so the most exposed of these; did win a good handicap last time
runners_data.spotlight: The most exposed of these after 11 runs over hurdles but it was win number four when returning to his best in a 2m5f Class 2 handicap at Kempton a month ago (hard fought; good ground); penalised accordingly and he might be vulnerable should one or two of these find the anticipated improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Le Beau Madrik and Legendary Luke will contest the early lead in this small field, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set an honest gallop from the outset. The prominent trio of Matty's Getaway, Padre Arthur, and the withdrawn Intosomethinggood would typically sit just behind, but with only four remaining runners, the pace will be straightforward rather than frantic. The two leaders will likely maintain a decent clip throughout the 2m5f journey, creating a test of stamina in the final half-mile. This shape favours horses with tactical speed who can stay close to the pace, as there's insufficient depth for hold-up horses to benefit from a strong finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dual Front Runner Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Le Beau Madrik and Legendary Luke both jump well and maintain their forward positions throughout
scenarios.body: The two leaders will engage in a prolonged battle from the home turn, with the winner being whoever has the most left in reserve. This sustained pace will suit the horse with superior stamina credentials and recent race fitness.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners go too fast early and begin to weaken approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: Matty's Getaway or Padre Arthur will inherit the lead late having conserved energy in behind the early pace. The winner will be the prominent runner with the best turn of foot when the leaders falter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders establishes a decisive advantage jumping the last and the field fails to respond
scenarios.body: Either Le Beau Madrik or Legendary Luke will dominate from the front, maintaining their advantage to the line. Superior jumping and race fitness will prove decisive in a performance that silences the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slower than expected and allows a patient ride to be effective
scenarios.body: A hold-up ride on one of the prominent horses could catch the leaders napping if they go too steadily early. The winner would need exceptional finishing speed to overcome the tactical disadvantage of this race shape.

watchPoints.text: Le Beau Madrik's jumping under pressure - any mistakes could be costly given his need to lead and sustain the gallop
Matty's Getaway's response to the tongue-tie - first-time headgear can be transformative but occasionally backfires
Legendary Luke's ability to settle if headed early - his front-running style may not suit if Le Beau Madrik takes him on from the start
The pace through the first mile - if too steady it could negate the natural advantages of the two confirmed leaders

races.name: Unibet Abram Mares' Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Girl Friday
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent form who should appreciate the step up in trip and good ground conditions.
runners_data.comment: She's raised in class with little experience behind her but clearly useful
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for £45,000 after winning a four-runner Irish mares' maiden point (3m, good); raced prominently and came home 4l to the good in a 2m3f maiden for mares at Wetherby; she's raised in class with little experience behind her but clearly useful.

runners_data.name: Great Dance
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs a strong pace to be effective but may find the ground faster than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Bred for this longer distance but she'd be a surprise winner; tongue-tie added
runners_data.spotlight: Won a weak bumper at Newton Abbot on debut but was then well held in a Listed race and the form of her close third on hurdle debut at Taunton is nothing to shout about (2m, good); bred for this far but she'd be a surprise winner; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: White Noise
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with proven class advantage but must overcome weight burden and recent heavy ground form.

runners_data.name: Torpille Dagrostis
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing cheekpieces again after making hard work of last win despite short odds.
runners_data.comment: It wasn't pretty in winning her maiden but her heart seems in the right place
runners_data.spotlight: Cheekpieces added for her last three races; it wasn't pretty when making hard work of justifying short odds in a Leopardstown maiden for mares in early March (2m5f, soft) but her heart seems in the right place and should run well again.

runners_data.name: Just A Glance
runners_data.note: Natural leader with unbeaten hurdles record who should stay this longer trip on breeding.
runners_data.comment: 2-2 over hurdles; should be fine over the longer distance but these terms are tough
runners_data.spotlight: Won a point bumper and followed up in a 2m4f maiden; unbeaten over hurdles after minor wins over 2m at Hereford (soft) and Chepstow (good to soft); should stay this longer trip fine but on the face of it these terms look tough.

runners_data.name: Dream Shadow
runners_data.note: Prominent performer who gets a 5lb weight swing with White Noise from their Warwick meeting.
runners_data.comment: 3m perhaps too far last time; previous run behind White Noise offers hope
runners_data.spotlight: Has just over 5l to find with White Noise on their Warwick clash in February (2m3f, heavy) but a 5lb pull with the winner can only help her cause and perhaps 3m on soft ground stretched her when a remote second at Doncaster (Listed); has to enter the reckoning.

runners_data.name: Livingonaprayer
runners_data.note: Proven over this trip with solid mares' novice wins but concerning pulled up effort last time out.
runners_data.comment: Dual winner; Doncaster was disappointing but probably wise to put a line through that
runners_data.spotlight: Won mares' novice races at Huntingdon (2m3f, good) and Wincanton (2m5f, good to soft) before pulling up when 18-1 for a Listed event at Doncaster (3m, soft); beaten too far out to blame the longer trip but it was a miserable day in South Yorkshire and plenty of horses underperformed on that card; could be given another chance.

runners_data.name: Millady
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner completely outclassed on ratings who needs everything to go right from the back.
runners_data.comment: Form of Hereford third gives her no right to be troubling the best of these
runners_data.spotlight: Improved to be third in a maiden at Hereford (2m3f, good) but that form gives her no right to be troubling the best of these.

races.paceDynamic: White Noise and Just A Glance will set the early pace in this Listed contest, with both confirmed front runners likely to contest the lead from the outset. Their presence ensures an honest gallop over this extended 2m5f trip, preventing any crawling pace that might disadvantage those who need a test of stamina. The prominent racers like Girl Friday, Torpille Dagrostis and Dream Shadow will track the leaders closely, while hold-up horses Great Dance and Millady may find themselves with too much ground to make up. This race shape favours prominent racers who can sit close enough to strike but avoid the early pace battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If White Noise and Just A Glance duel early and tie up over this stamina-sapping trip
scenarios.body: The pace-setters weaken in the final half-mile, allowing those who raced handily behind to sweep past with superior finishing kicks. Girl Friday and Dream Shadow are perfectly positioned to capitalize from their prominent berths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets first run and the other folds early
scenarios.body: White Noise or Just A Glance secures uncontested control and uses superior class to repel late challenges over this staying trip. The lack of early pressure allows the leader to save energy for a strong finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Artist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple leaders going at it
scenarios.body: A furious gallop plays into the hands of those held up, as the pace collapses dramatically in the closing stages. Great Dance gets the perfect setup to unleash a decisive late run from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference disrupts the favourites' chances
scenarios.body: The race develops unexpectedly with fallers or mistakes creating opportunities for unfancied runners to capitalize. Livingonaprayer or Millady could sneak through when others hit trouble.

watchPoints.text: White Noise may struggle with the 161lbs burden if the early pace becomes genuinely strong against Just A Glance
Great Dance needs the leaders to go too fast early to get her hold-up style into the race from the rear
Torpille Dagrostis has cheekpieces applied again after her unconvincing last win at short odds
Just A Glance is unbeaten over hurdles but faces a significant class test in this Listed company
Dream Shadow gets a helpful 5lb swing with White Noise from their previous encounter at Warwick

races.name: Unibet Silver Trophy Handicap Chase (Grade 2) (A Limited Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Outlaw Peter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who thrived in new cheekpieces when winning over C&D just 11 days ago, but quick turnaround could catch up
runners_data.comment: Back up 6lb for his clearcut recent win in the Middle Distance Veterans' Final over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple winner who reacted well to the new cheekpieces when a clearcut winner of the Middle Distance Veterans' Final over C&D only 11 days ago; historically well treated despite the 6lb rise but there's a suspicion that younger limbs this time may have his measure.

runners_data.name: Fugitif
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form but trainer Henry Hobson's 0/3 record in last 14 days raises questions about current stable form

runners_data.name: Tommy's Oscar
runners_data.note: Strong closer who proved effective at 3m last time but this shorter trip on good ground should suit his two-mile background better
runners_data.comment: The drop back in trip is no cause for concern but a 5lb rise for that last win has to be
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who made his name as a two-miler and the slow pace helped when making his first foray over 3m a successful one at Carlisle (good to soft; effective on good); solid second the run before over 2m4f but a 5lb rise for last time could be troublesome.

runners_data.name: Bleu d'Enfer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying just 147lbs but his recent form shows decline from earlier seasonal promise

runners_data.name: The Bluesman
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse with strong finishing kick who won twice earlier this season and suits this tactical setup perfectly

runners_data.name: Riskintheground
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won this race 12 months ago but his form nosedived badly after that Cheltenham success
runners_data.comment: Won this last year off 1lb higher and signs of returning to form last time at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race 12 months ago at Cheltenham when 1lb higher so he's dangerously handicapped for his defence; his form had nosedived after winning in a small field at Newton Abbot in October but the signs were more encouraging last time in the 2m4f Plate at the Festival as he was staying on when hampered by a faller at the last fence; has to be of interest, especially given the yard's form.

runners_data.name: Triple Trade
runners_data.note: Patient ride specialist who won twice this season but his early departure over C&D 11 days ago creates slight fitness doubt
runners_data.comment: Early casualty here 11 days ago; has a lot in his favour so merits each-way consideration
runners_data.spotlight: Still on a good mark despite winning twice this season (2m/2m4f; soft/good) and was 11-2 for the veterans' final over C&D earlier this month, only to depart early; has a lot in his favour so merits each-way consideration.

runners_data.name: Jour d'Evasion
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner who could get uncontested lead but his three wins this season all came over shorter trips

runners_data.name: Mousey Brown
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from 81-day break with questions about wellbeing after recent hurdle efforts
runners_data.comment: Irish raider for whom trip/ground is ideal; revival needed but cheekpieces are new
runners_data.spotlight: Has faced stiff tasks over hurdles on her last two starts in races won by Wodhooh and Feet Of A Dancer; has a bit to prove on the wellbeing front as her runs before those (chasing and hurdling) weren't her best, but both her chase wins have been on good ground at about this trip and this Irish raider now goes in cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Moon d'Orange
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose new visor worked well at Cheltenham but remains winless in 10 attempts since 2023
runners_data.comment: The new visor worked well when a never-nearer third in the Plate last month
runners_data.spotlight: 9lb higher when beaten 3.5l by Riskintheground 12 months ago; 0-10 in the meantime but the new visor worked well when a never-nearer third in the Plate at Cheltenham last month and clear claims if he can back that up.

runners_data.name: Zurich
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who would prefer this race back at Cheltenham where he won in October on similar good ground
runners_data.comment: Had a good season and his fifth in last month's Plate at Cheltenham was admirable
runners_data.spotlight: Could have done without this race being transferred from Cheltenham as he won there in October (good ground) and stayed on well for fifth in last month's Plate; his run in between at Doncaster in a race that's worked out well was also admirable; every chance.

races.paceDynamic: Jour d'Evasion will lead unchallenged early with Outlaw Peter and Zurich tracking prominently, but no genuine pace pressure means moderate fractions through the first mile. The large pack of hold-up horses (Tommy's Oscar, Fugitif, The Bluesman, Riskintheground, Triple Trade, Mousey Brown, Moon d'Orange) will bunch up behind, setting up a cavalry charge from 4f out. With one soft leader and eight closers, this creates a classic tactical scramble where patient rides and strong finishing kicks become crucial. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing speed over 2m4f.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Stampede
scenarios.trigger: If Jour d'Evasion sets modest fractions and the field stays bunched until late
scenarios.body: The patient brigade gets perfect delivery with Tommy's Oscar and The Bluesman having every chance to unleash their finishing speed. Multiple closers converge simultaneously, favouring horses with the strongest final 2f kick over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Outlaw Peter or Zurich move off the pace earlier than expected to pressure Jour d'Evasion
scenarios.body: The race develops more honest fractions that stretch the field earlier, playing to horses positioned handily rather than those needing the perfect setup. Outlaw Peter's recent C&D win and Zurich's Cheltenham form become more relevant in a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Stalemate Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys wait too long in the pack and leave finishing too late
scenarios.body: The moderate pace becomes a complete crawl with everyone still in contention at the 2f marker, creating a messy sprint finish. Horses drawn best or with the clearest runs benefit most from the resulting traffic problems and interference.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Jour d'Evasion gets an uncontested lead and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The early leader maintains honest gallop throughout and proves tough to pass when the closers finally mount their challenge. His three wins this season including over this C&D suggest he could defy the tactical odds.

watchPoints.text: Jour d'Evasion could steal a march if given uncontested lead with Outlaw Peter and Zurich failing to apply early pressure
Tommy's Oscar and The Bluesman both need clear runs in final 2f as eight hold-up horses create potential traffic problems
Outlaw Peter's 11-day turnaround after hard-fought C&D win could see stamina reserves depleted in closing stages
Triple Trade's early fall over C&D recently means any jumping errors today could prove costly given his hold-up style
Moon d'Orange's new visor worked at Cheltenham but this trainer John McConnell is 0/19 in last 14 days

races.name: Try Unibets Smartview Racecards Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Huffin An A Puffin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong recent form but faces tougher opposition than recent Doncaster win
runners_data.comment: The defeat of Storming George now looks good; excuses last time; had wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Newbury novice hurdle in March 2024 (for Harry Derham) and returned from a long absence to make successful stable/handicap debut at Doncaster (2m3f, soft), beating none other than last week's Grade 1 winner Storming George; was found to be coughing after pulling up off this 3lb higher mark at Newbury (2m4f; favourite); interesting after wind surgery; should be well handicapped.

runners_data.name: La Pinsonniere
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist from top yard with consistent form, headgear change could sharpen her up
runners_data.comment: Likeably consistent and was third of 13 off this mark over Kempton's 2m5f a month ago
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in a Listed hurdle for mares at this fixture (Cheltenham) 12 months ago; only 1-12 but she's likeably consistent and was third of 13 off this mark over Kempton's 2m5f a month ago (good) having been given every chance; solid claims once more.

runners_data.name: Royal Infantry
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse for in-form Skelton team, likes to come from behind with strong finish

runners_data.name: Norman Fletcher
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but distance stretches his stamina limits based on recent Bangor effort
runners_data.comment: Wasn't that strong through the line over Bangor's extended 2m3f last time
runners_data.spotlight: All five wins have been at about 2m or 2m1f; wasn't that strong through the line over Bangor's extended 2m3f last time (good) and has further to go here; tries cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Irandando Has
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from small yard with limited recent experience, 32 days off concerning

runners_data.name: Idy Wood
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner seeking redemption after two poor runs, needs to bounce back to form
runners_data.comment: Capable 8yo but on a recovery mission after finishing tailed on his last two starts
runners_data.spotlight: Won over fences last season and has won twice over hurdles since September; now he's on a recovery mission after very quiet runs at Windsor (2m4f) and at the Cheltenham Festival (3m; again on his favoured good ground).

runners_data.name: Below The Radar
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up type from champion yard, consistent placer who could benefit from strong pace

runners_data.name: Le Tiep's Sacre
runners_data.note: Promising young prominent runner making only second handicap start after long absence
runners_data.comment: Ran well to be fifth on handicap debut when entitled to need the race after a year off
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo; won a Fontwell maiden last March (2m1f, good to soft) and first sighting since then when beaten a shade over 3l on last month's handicap debut at Kempton; looked threatening until perhaps a lack of match sharpness told late on; in the mix.

runners_data.name: George's Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 110 days off, distance suits but fitness questioned
runners_data.comment: Needs to settle better than at Kempton; retains potential at this trip; had wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Has only won a maiden but there has been promise in his handicap runs and he caught the attention of the stewards when trying this far for the first time at Kempton on Boxing Day (good; off since); he did take a fierce hold on that occasion and will need to settle better here, but still interesting on the back of a wind operation.

runners_data.name: Johnson's Blue
runners_data.note: Front-runner with questions over current form after tailed-off hurdle run and poor chase efforts
runners_data.comment: Potentially on a useful mark if he can get back on track, but there are risks attached
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off on his final hurdle start in November and three subsequent chase runs leave him with further questions to answer; potentially on a useful mark if he can get back on track, but there are clearly risks attached.

runners_data.name: Masked Dance
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form but faces significant step up in class from recent wins
runners_data.comment: Highly likely to run another solid race but this is stronger than she's accustomed to
runners_data.spotlight: Better than ever in her last three starts over 2m5f and 3m; highly likely to run another solid race but this is stronger than she's accustomed to.

runners_data.name: Analiese
runners_data.note: Lightly raced prominent runner with upward trajectory, only five-year-old in field could improve
runners_data.comment: Progressive mare who has won three of her last four races; up just 3lb for the latest
runners_data.spotlight: Sole defeat in her last four races came at the hands of a progressive horse at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft); shrugged aside that minor blip with a workmanlike win at Chepstow (2m3f, soft); 3lb rise isn't the end of the world.

races.paceDynamic: Idy Wood and Johnson's Blue will force early pace with Huffin An A Puffin, Norman Fletcher, Le Tiep's Sacre, Masked Dance and Analiese all wanting prominent positions behind. This creates serious congestion in the first half-mile before the field strings out. The dual front-runners should ensure an honest gallop over this staying trip, but the bottleneck of prominent runners creates tactical danger at the business end. This pace dynamic strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early scramble and pick off tired leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong and prominent runners get shuffled back
scenarios.body: The dual pace-setters tire and the congested prominent pack gets compromised, allowing patient hold-up runners to sweep through late. Royal Infantry and La Pinsonniere benefit most from their patient tactics and strong finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tactical win
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner gets the perfect position behind the leaders
scenarios.body: A horse like Huffin An A Puffin or Analiese avoids the early congestion and times their challenge perfectly as the front-runners weaken. Their tactical speed proves decisive in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner survival
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is more measured than expected
scenarios.body: Idy Wood or Johnson's Blue get softer sectionals early and have enough left to repel late challengers. The lack of early pressure allows them to dictate throughout and hold on grimly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners go off too fast and burn out early
scenarios.body: The dual pace-setters cook themselves and the prominent pack also suffers from the early burn-up. A patient hold-up horse with stamina reserves comes from last to first in a slow-motion finish.

watchPoints.text: Johnson's Blue could fold quickly if not bouncing back to form, leaving Idy Wood isolated on the lead
Traffic problems likely at the third-last hurdle with Norman Fletcher, Masked Dance and Le Tiep's Sacre all wanting the same prominent spot
George's Lad returning from 110-day absence may need the run despite Emma Lavelle's 2/13 recent record
La Pinsonniere wearing new headgear for Henderson team suggests they expect improvement from consistent mare
Huffin An A Puffin faces much stronger field than when winning at Doncaster last time out

races.name: Try Unibets New Racing Betbuilder Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ki Woo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making debut for new yard after 41-day break, likely to be pace-setter but may lack race fitness

runners_data.name: Holokea
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer with strong recent chase form, particularly effective when getting patient ride from Sean Bowen
runners_data.comment: Mown down late on in big field at Windsor (extended 3m4f, soft) in January three runs back
runners_data.spotlight: Won bumper and maiden hurdle when on good ground; scored at Ffos Las (3m1f, soft) in October and runner-up in four of his other six chases, including when mown down late on in a big field at Windsor (extended 3m4f, soft) in January; ran poorly over C&D next time and well beaten at Cheltenham Festival on latest but both those races were much warmer than this.

runners_data.name: Regarde
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up horse returning after wind operations and 144-day break, won over course and distance on good ground
runners_data.comment: Won over C&D (good) last March; has a good record when returning from a break; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Has had three wind operations, two of them last year; won four-runner race over C&D (good) when upped in trip last March and ran creditably on next two starts; not disgraced at Ascot in November when last seen; has a good record when returning from a break, so goes on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Red Delta
runners_data.note: Proven extreme stayer who won 3m4f Lincolnshire National, suits prominent position and handles good ground well
runners_data.comment: Stays thoroughly and latest start (3m/hampered) can be forgiven; considered back at 3m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Stays thoroughly, having won the Lincolnshire National at Market Rasen (3m4f) on Boxing Day and performed well in the Eider at Newcastle (4m1f) in February; perhaps his heavy defeat over 3m on latest start can therefore be forgiven, particularly as he was hampered early on; considered back at 3m4f.

runners_data.name: Yes Day
runners_data.note: Prominent runner now 13lb below peak rating and showing declining form, struggled on good ground last time
runners_data.comment: Below form this term and didn't show much on good ground latest; won over 3m7f last March
runners_data.spotlight: He's now 13lb below his peak mark but hasn't been at his best this season and didn't show much when back on good ground (3m) three weeks ago; won over 3m7f last March but there may be more solid options.

runners_data.name: Some Scope
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up horse wearing first-time visor, back in form after second at Newbury on latest start
runners_data.comment: Has a competitive mark but his inconsistency and going beyond 3m2f both introduce doubts
runners_data.spotlight: Won from the front in first-time visor (kept since) at Doncaster in December; back to form when second at Newbury on latest start, his second run after his second wind operation; has a competitive mark but his inconsistency and going beyond 3m2f both introduce doubts.

runners_data.name: Fierce Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from top yard but stepping up to longest trip yet, previous best was 3m2f victory
runners_data.comment: Furthest he's been is 3m2f when rallying to beat Red Delta at Doncaster (soft) in November
runners_data.spotlight: The furthest he's been was 3m2f when he rallied to win from Red Delta in a small field at Doncaster (soft; made most) in November; something amiss next time but he was back on song for second at Carlisle (3m, good to soft; probably effective on good) on latest outing, making it good runs on both his starts in cheekpieces; up 2lb but needs a close look.

runners_data.name: Gold Emery
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent place record but has never won over fences, all career runs on softer ground
runners_data.comment: Running creditably and stays, but no win from 16 attempts over fences (runner-up in seven)
runners_data.spotlight: All starts on softer than good; no win from 16 attempts over fences but runner-up in seven, including off this mark when he tried an extended 3m6f in the North Wales National at Bangor on penultimate start; ran creditably over 3m7f at Chepstow latest, so has place claims again but he does not look the percentage call for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Fortunedefortunata
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making debut for new trainer after poor season, fell here last time and major question marks
runners_data.comment: Out of form for Gordon Elliott; fell mid-race here 11 days ago on debut for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Mostly campaigned in competitive staying chases when with Gordon Elliott and did not accomplish much this season; £3,000 buy in February but fell mid-race here 11 days ago on debut for new yard; cheekpieces (tried once) return; major questions to answer.

runners_data.name: The Grey Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer from small yard with recent wins on heavy ground, unproven on good surface

runners_data.name: Bodhisattva
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing visor, finished third in Edinburgh National but heavy defeats since suggest decline
runners_data.comment: Stays well; heavy defeats on last three outings but soft ground may not have been ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Third of five finishers in the 3m7f Edinburgh National at Musselburgh in February, which wasn't as good as his second in the same race in 2025; heavy defeats on last three outings but soft ground may not have been ideal.

races.paceDynamic: Ki Woo will be the natural pace-setter from his prominent style, with Red Delta, Yes Day, Fierce Warrior, Gold Emery and Some Scope all capable of racing close to the pace early. This creates a scenario where multiple horses want similar positions, likely resulting in steady to strong galloping through the middle sections over this staying trip. The presence of several hold-up horses like Holokea, Regarde, Some Scope, Fortunedefortunata, The Grey Man and Bodhisattva suggests the pace will be solid enough to set up a finish. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can benefit from the solid pace and produce their customary late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners maintain a solid gallop through the extended middle sections
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will perfectly set up the race for the patient hold-up performers who can unleash their finishing kicks. Horses like Holokea, Regarde and Some Scope can time their challenges perfectly in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runners control
scenarios.trigger: If Ki Woo gets an easy lead and the pace becomes pedestrian early
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the pace-setters to dictate terms and save energy for a sustained finish. Ki Woo and Red Delta can use their stamina to grind out the finish when the hold-up horses lack the pace to make up ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midrace pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too hard early and come back to the field dramatically
scenarios.body: The early exertions take their toll and create a stop-start rhythm that doesn't suit anyone perfectly. This opens the door for a horse with tactical speed like Some Scope or an improver getting a perfect trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina test develops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine throughout and becomes a true staying test
scenarios.body: The extended trip and solid gallop finds out any horses lacking true stamina over this extreme distance. Only the proven stayers with the best recent form can cope with the relentless demands.

watchPoints.text: Ki Woo making yard debut after long break could either set perfect pace or lack race fitness to sustain effort
Gold Emery has never raced on good ground and could struggle with the faster surface conditions
Some Scope in first-time visor has shown renewed form and could benefit from the expected strong pace
Regarde returning after 144-day layoff following wind operations, fitness must be taken on trust
The Grey Man and Bodhisattva both need the pace to collapse to get competitive, watch for early positioning

races.name: Read Nicky Hendersons Unibet Blog Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Moon Rocket
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 34-day break with inconsistent recent form, needs to lead but fitness question mark

runners_data.name: Red Risk
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid Pertemps form, 11-year-old retains ability but Paddy Hanlon's 5lb claim helps
runners_data.comment: Uttoxeter was disappointing but he's shown bouncebackability in the past
runners_data.spotlight: Retains lots of ability despite his advancing years and won a Pertemps qualifier at Musselburgh in February (3m, good to soft); Uttoxeter was disappointing in a race he won the previous year, but he's shown bouncebackability in the past.

runners_data.name: Serious Chat
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with excellent course record (4W8P from 14 runs on similar going), strong handicap profile
runners_data.comment: Probably ran as well as he ever has when beaten half a length at Doncaster last time
runners_data.spotlight: The winner of three handicaps, at 2m7f, 2m6f and 2m3f; probably ran as well as he ever has when beaten half a length at Doncaster last time (3m, soft); thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Lord Snootie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner showing improved form recently, 1-17 record poor but second at Bangor suggests return to form
runners_data.comment: His best run for ages when a rallying second at Bangor last month; weighted to win races
runners_data.spotlight: Only 1-17 but has flashes of smart form in good handicaps and easily his best run for ages when a rallying second at Bangor last month (2m7f, good; effective on softer); weighted to win races and seriously considered.

runners_data.name: Red Dirt Road
runners_data.note: Front-runner with mixed recent form, 4-12 over hurdles but tendency to fade late over this trip
runners_data.comment: A sitting duck when ridden prominently in the Pertemps Final; better can be expected
runners_data.spotlight: He can have his off days but he's 4-12 over hurdles and he ran well to be fourth in a Pertemps qualifier over C&D before dropping out in the final furlong after racing up with the pace; he was always likely to prove a sitting duck when it mattered at Cheltenham and better can be expected here.

runners_data.name: Firestream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form Chester Williams, first-time cheekpieces last time showed promise after long absence
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced at nine; good run last time and chance if the wheels can stay on
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden/handicap wins for Anthony Honeyball; long absences a feature in his profile but there were positives at Uttoxeter last month (2m4f, soft; first-time cheekpieces) where he ran well for a long way; stays this far; chance if the wheels can stay on.

runners_data.name: Dartan
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 180-day break, tends to fade in finish but first-time visor may help
runners_data.comment: Early days with this yard but appears to have developed some of his own ideas
runners_data.spotlight: Useful hurdler in Ireland; beaten in a match over fences on stable debut (first-time visor); this return to hurdles is welcomed but he appears to have developed some of his own ideas; had wind surgery.

runners_data.name: Smokeringinthedark
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form recently, 15-day turnaround and strong trainer record (9/11) are positives

runners_data.name: Kilwaughter
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with amateur jockey, 7lb rise after Newbury win but Mr Stenhouse knows him well
runners_data.comment: 7lb rise for last time seems harsh enough but he'll probably improve again for going 3m
runners_data.spotlight: Smart in bumpers and getting there over hurdles after digging deep for a successful handicap debut under Jack Stenhouse at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft); 7lb rise seems harsh enough but he'll probably improve again for going 3m.

runners_data.name: King Of The Lake
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with poor trainer form (0/11), 33-1 last time suggests confidence lacking
runners_data.comment: He was a 33-1 chance last month at Uttoxeter and he ran like one
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins in 2025 and now only 2lb higher than for the last of those at Chepstow in December (2m7f, good to soft); however, he was a 33-1 chance last month at Uttoxeter and he ran like one.

races.paceDynamic: Moon Rocket and Red Dirt Road will contest the early lead, with Red Dirt Road likely to dominate given his more consistent front-running profile. Four prominent runners (Red Risk, Serious Chat, Lord Snootie, Firestream) will create congestion behind the leaders, setting up traffic problems approaching the business end. The honest gallop will stretch the field over this extended trip, but the two hold-up horses (Smokeringinthedark, Kilwaughter) face a significant disadvantage with limited late pace to close into. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can secure good positions early and avoid the midfield scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not suicidal, allowing prominent runners to stay in touch
scenarios.body: The leaders will weaken in the final half-mile, setting up perfectly for a prominent runner to strike approaching the last. Traffic issues will hamper those stuck midfield while the pace won't be strong enough for hold-up horses to close effectively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Rocket or Red Dirt Road can dictate at a sensible pace without fierce early pressure
scenarios.body: The leader will have enough left to resist late challenges, particularly with the extended trip suiting a patient front-running approach. Hold-up horses will find the pace too steady to mount effective closing efforts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with both leaders going hard from the start
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will collapse the field in the final furlong, creating the perfect scenario for patient hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders. Smokeringinthedark and Kilwaughter will benefit from the strongest pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems severely hamper the prominent runners and the pace becomes messy
scenarios.body: A horse settling further back but not relying on pure hold-up tactics will find the clearest passage when others are stopped for room. The compromised runs of fancied prominent runners will open the door.

watchPoints.text: Red Dirt Road and Moon Rocket setting too strong an early pace will compromise both front-runners
Traffic problems developing 2-3 out as four prominent runners (Red Risk, Serious Chat, Lord Snootie, Firestream) converge
Smokeringinthedark needing the leaders to go hard early to set up his hold-up style over this extended trip
Dartan's fitness after 180-day absence and whether the first-time visor prevents his usual late fade
Red Risk's jumping under pressure given his 11-year-old legs over this demanding distance

races.name: Unibet Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hang In There
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with highest OR (151) but at 12 years old needs everything to fall right and 46 days since last run could leave him short.
runners_data.comment: Encouraging third at Newbury last time and this ground should be more suitable
runners_data.spotlight: Strike-rate of 9-27 over fences and his third in a veterans' chase at Newbury in February (3m2f) was encouraging given he had been absent for three months and good to soft ground would have been slow enough; should run well.

runners_data.name: Iron Bridge
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form but poor 2-17 strike rate over fences creates trust issues despite obvious ability.
runners_data.comment: Strong stayer but with a strike-rate of only 2-17 over fences and excuses are wearing thin
runners_data.spotlight: A strong stayer but with a strike-rate of only 2-17 over fences and excuses are wearing thin; on the plus side, they were solid enough efforts on last two starts (3m4f/3m6f) and he nearly won off this mark on his reappearance (3m2f).

runners_data.name: Bhaloo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 137-day break with all-or-nothing profile that's produced nothing recently under Henderson.
runners_data.comment: Even if back on song after a break his form figures at 3m or beyond are PPP
runners_data.spotlight: All-or-nothing profile and it's been nothing on his last two starts, while even if he was able to rediscover some spark after another break, his form figures at 3m or beyond are PPP; hardly the safest option.

runners_data.name: Millforce
runners_data.note: Switches from Cromwell to Oliver after 171-day absence, prominent style but needs to prove Irish form translates back to Britain.
runners_data.comment: Absent since October when he signed off for Gavin Cromwell with a 2m6f win at Galway
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since October when he signed off for Gavin Cromwell with a 2m6f win at Galway (yielding); stays 3m and should get this far, but would need to see some confidence behind him.

runners_data.name: Egbert
runners_data.note: Course winner who can lead or hold up, proven on good ground here but jumping errors are a glaring concern despite recent wins.
runners_data.comment: 2-2 here but the glaring concern is his nothing run at Exeter last time
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner in December 2024 (heavy; won on good) and made it 2-2 here when beating three rivals over 3m4f (good to soft) on reappearance; the glaring concern is his nothing run at Exeter last time when in trouble a long way out.

runners_data.name: Hold Your Fort
runners_data.note: Front-runner coming off Ascot win where he dominated from the front, though quality of opposition was questionable.
runners_data.comment: Dominated his two rivals from the front at Ascot (3m, good); up 5lb; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Did well in the autumn and won again last month at Ascot (3m, good) where he dominated his two rivals from the front; there's a suspicion that his two rivals underperformed and he's 5lb higher here, but still considered.

runners_data.name: Grand Geste
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins at this course recently but National Hunt Chase flop at Cheltenham raises stamina questions.
runners_data.comment: Strong form claims back on his favourite track; good ground would be a slight concern
runners_data.spotlight: Suffered two flops in his last three races but the latest was in the National Hunt Chase at Cheltenham; both wins since December have been here (3m1f/3m4f), latterly in the 11-runner Grand National Trial that always takes some winning; if on a going day then he would have strong claims, for all that softer ground would be preferred.

runners_data.name: Minella Crooner
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter but form has been poor since leaving Elliott's yard and represents significant risk at current prices.
runners_data.comment: Left Gordon Elliott on a downer and has continued in similar vein for current team
runners_data.spotlight: Once very smart for Gordon Elliott but left that yard on a downer and has continued in similar vein for current team; too risky at the minute.

races.paceDynamic: Minella Crooner and Hold Your Fort are the likeliest pace-setters, with Iron Bridge, Bhaloo, Grand Geste and Millforce tracking prominently in the early stages. Hold Your Fort showed front-running tactics when winning at Ascot last month and will likely press Minella Crooner for the lead, creating a solid but not destructive gallop over this stamina-sapping trip. The pace should be testing enough to find out the non-stayers but controlled enough that the leaders won't collapse, meaning prominent racers who can quicken from close range will have the tactical edge over hold-up horses who need the pace to collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Hold Your Fort and Minella Crooner set sustainable fractions and aren't pressed hard early
scenarios.body: The leaders kick clear turning for home as the hold-up horses struggle to close the gap on good ground over this stamina test. Front-running tactics prove decisive as the pace doesn't collapse enough for closers to be effective.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is solid but one of the prominent racers has enough left to quicken
scenarios.body: Iron Bridge or Grand Geste can sit handy, let the leaders do the work, then strike approaching the last two fences. Their class tells in a finish where stamina and tactical position both matter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Veteran's Experience Tells
scenarios.trigger: If Hang In There gets the right pace setup and finds his old spark from off the pace
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old's superior class rating comes to the fore as the race develops into a stamina test that suits his patient style. His hold-up tactics work when the leaders weaken in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early and tie up in the straight
scenarios.body: The front-runners pay for their exuberance as Hang In There and other hold-up horses storm home in the final furlong. The good going helps the closers' turn of foot become effective late on.

watchPoints.text: Watch Egbert's jumping at the early fences as his recent fall and tendency to make errors could end his chance early despite home course advantage.
Watch how aggressively Hold Your Fort goes forward as his front-running tactics worked at Ascot but stronger pace pressure here could expose stamina limits.
Watch Iron Bridge's position turning for home as he needs to be close enough to strike but has disappointed when well-placed before.
Watch Hang In There's position at halfway as the 12-year-old needs the leaders to go hard enough to come back to him in the straight.
Watch the early pace between Minella Crooner and Hold Your Fort as their battle for the lead will determine whether closers get into the race.

races.name: Unibet Pony Racing Authority Graduates Handicap Hurdle (Conditional Jockeys' And Amateur Riders')

runners_data.name: Count Of Vendome
runners_data.note: Front-running style perfectly suited to small field with recent winning form over this trip giving him tactical advantage

runners_data.name: Vocito
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 147-day break which could either freshen him up or leave him needing the run badly
runners_data.comment: Exposed but could be all the better for a break and he's on his last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner over hurdles but exposed and was performing no more than okay when last seen in November; however, he could be all the better for a break and he's on his last winning mark.

runners_data.name: Lively Citizen
runners_data.note: Proven over hurdles with prominent style ideal for tracking the leaders but switches back from disappointing chase efforts
runners_data.comment: There's a big run in him back over hurdles if he can get his act together
runners_data.spotlight: Very capable over fences but pulled up in that discipline on his last two starts following a break of 217 days; he did go close over hurdles at Aintree three runs ago so there's a big effort in him if he can get his act together.

runners_data.name: Brendas Asking
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces positioning challenge but has class edge returning from long 357-day absence for strong stable
runners_data.comment: Has the form to feature off this mark if on her game after a year out
runners_data.spotlight: Won a handicap hurdle at Ludlow in October 2024 (2m, good) and the following April a novice back at the same venue, after flying too high at the Cheltenham Festival; has the form to feature off this mark if on her game after a year out.

runners_data.name: Scintillante
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner returning from 185-day break who needs strong early pace to set up his finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Outclassed on final run in October; he had been running well prior to that
runners_data.spotlight: 5lb out of the weights and 50-1 when well beaten in the Welsh Champion Hurdle on final run in October; his earlier races were more realistic than that and he ran well; solid chance if fitness doesn't hold him back.

runners_data.name: Across Earth
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with good recent form who should get ideal trip tracking the early leaders
runners_data.comment: It was a pretty good handicap in which he went down narrowly at Newbury the last time
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent for a while now and, although beaten off this mark on his last two starts, it was a pretty good handicap in which he went down narrowly at Newbury the last time (2m, good to soft); thereabouts if gelling with Jude Fernandes.

runners_data.name: Innamorato
runners_data.note: Promising type for expanding Paul Nicholls stable whose prominent style suits the likely race shape well
runners_data.comment: Probably improving and interesting on handicap debut if okay on this quicker ground
runners_data.spotlight: Placed on the Flat and over hurdles in France; it was a quiet start for Paul Nicholls but came good in a heavy-ground maiden at Taunton (2m3f) and then ran third in a slowly run race at Newbury (good to soft; form franked); open to improvement in a race of this nature (handicap debut), though he did swerve a recent Ascot engagement on account of good ground so watch the weather.

races.paceDynamic: Count Of Vendome and Vocito will contest the early lead, with Count Of Vendome's recent front-running form making him likely to dictate terms from the outset. The pace should be honest rather than frantic given only two confirmed leaders in an 8-runner field, allowing the race to develop into a tactical affair from halfway. The prominent runners Lively Citizen, Across Earth and Innamorato will track the leaders closely, while the hold-up horses Brendas Asking and Scintillante face the challenge of making up ground in the final stages. This shape clearly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed, as they can position perfectly behind the leaders and strike when the pace inevitably quickens approaching the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is steady allowing tactical positioning
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get the perfect trip tracking the two leaders before making their move at the business end. Those who can sit handy and quicken have every chance to exploit their ideal racing position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Count Of Vendome maintains his recent front-running form and sees off challenges
scenarios.body: The proven leader uses his fitness advantage and tactical position to control the race throughout. His recent winning form over the trip gives him every chance to repeat the dose from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong and the leaders come back to the field
scenarios.body: The sustained early pace sets up perfectly for Brendas Asking and Scintillante to unleash late runs. Both have the class to capitalize if the front-runners weaken in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long Layoff Success
scenarios.trigger: If Vocito's 147-day break proves beneficial rather than detrimental
scenarios.body: The extended rest has recharged Vocito who uses his class and front-running ability to spring a surprise. His four hurdles wins show he has the talent if the freshness works in his favor.

watchPoints.text: Watch Count Of Vendome's jumping under pressure as he tries to lead throughout against Vocito's early challenge
Monitor how quickly Vocito settles after his long layoff as any keen tendencies could compromise his stamina reserves
Brendas Asking and Scintillante both face serious positioning concerns from wide draws if the early pace proves moderate
Observe Lively Citizen's attitude after two disappointing chase runs as confidence could be fragile switching back to hurdles
Track Across Earth's position entering the straight as he needs to be within striking distance to use his proven finishing kick
